subject: Hentati et al. (1992)
object: Hentati et al. (1992) studied 2 CMT2 pedigrees and excluded the CMT2 locus from the chromosome 17 region where CMT1A maps (lod score -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58). In a CMT1 pedigree studied alongside them, CMT1A linkage was confirmed (lod +3.67 at theta = 0.00). Negative lod scores were also obtained in CMT2 for the chromosome 1 region containing CMT1B (lod -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61).

subject: Hentati et al. (1992)
object: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous. They found that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.

subject: Ben Othmane et al. (1993)
object: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) performed pedigree linkage analysis in 6 large autosomal dominant CMT2 families and demonstrated linkage to microsatellite markers D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228, and D1S199 in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1. Multipoint analysis of the linked families placed the CMT2A gene most likely within the interval flanked by D1S244 and D1S228, with odds of approximately 70:1 for lying within versus outside that interval.

subject: Ben Othmane et al. (1993)
object: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity among 6 CMT2 families using admixture analysis of two-point lod scores, supported by multipoint admixture analysis. Three families (DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523) had posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 of being of the linked type. The authors suggested that the CMT2 phenotype results from at least 2 different genes.

subject: Ben Othmane et al. (1993)
object: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) described CMT2 as an inherited peripheral neuropathy with variable age of onset and normal or slightly reduced nerve conduction velocity, distinct pathologically and genetically from CMT1.

subject: Saito et al. (1997)
object: Saito et al. (1997) performed linkage analysis in 2 Japanese families with CMT2 and obtained a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at marker D1S244, consistent with linkage to the CMT2A locus on chromosome 1p35-p36.

subject: Saito et al. (1997)
object: Saito et al. (1997) excluded the CMT2B and CMT2D loci in the 2 Japanese CMT2 families by linkage analysis with markers D3S1551, D3S1290, and D7S484.

subject: Saito et al. (1997)
object: Saito et al. (1997) described the clinical features of CMT2A in 2 Japanese families. The posterior and anterior tibial muscles were similarly weak. Tendon reflexes were preserved in the upper limbs but reduced or absent in the lower limbs. The peripheral nerves were not enlarged, and only 20% of affected individuals had mild sensory disturbance.

subject: Zhao et al. (2001)
object: Zhao et al. (2001) found a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene in patients with CMT2A, a disorder previously mapped to an interval that contains KIF1B. They concluded that defects in axonal transport caused by a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.

subject: Zhao et al. (2001)
object: Zhao et al. (2001) reported that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from apnea caused by nervous system defects, and that knockout neurons dying in culture could be rescued by expressing the KIF1B-beta isoform. Heterozygous mice had a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and developed progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.

subject: Zhao et al. (2001)
object: Zhao et al. (2001) described KIF1B-beta, an isoform of the kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B that differs from KIF1B in its cargo-binding domain. KIF1B had previously been shown to transport mitochondria.
